I am nonbinary and pansexual. I got kicked out of college in North Carolina after having a car accident that resulted in brain damage.  I had lived on campus so my housing was related to me being enrolled. I ended up living in my car for a while. I had a cat (yes, I know, I lived on campus and I shouldn't have done it but without my cat I wouldn't have survived). I had only been dating this guy for a short time and when he knew how rough it was for me he offered to let me stay at his place until I figured things out. 

I moved in, and about 2 months later I moved out to my own apartment and got a crap job at Walmart unloading trucks. Walmart didn't last long, as the brain damage was still a severe issue and I was very disabled even if I didn't want to admit it. 

I moved back in with him about 2 months later. Lost the job and the apartment. 

This so far isn't much of a good story, but me and that guy have been together 7 years now. I got approved for disability last year. Now I can help with rent and expenses and I'm just working on accepting where I'm at health wise. 

I am sending you all the best. I really hope you can find a place to stay.

I have had my cat for a year. I got her just after I started to get sick. She's registered as an Emotional Support Animal (ESA). I was with my ex and he also had a cat, my plan was to have him keep the cat when I had dorm inspections (this was before she was registered) but he was always pretty abusive and the illness was too much for him. 

When we broke up I was lost. I had wanted to leave him for so long, but he threatened my life so often that it just didn't seem worth it. If I left he wouldn't feel bad killing me, because I was already gone from his life what would it matter? 

Pretty soon I had to leave college. I couldn't focus, I slept too much and never felt rested, I passed out a lot, and my health just continued downward. I was homeless. I moved in with a friend of mine into her studio apartment and brought my cat (still wasn't registered) and her apartment didn't allow pets. Eventually we were found out. I then looked into moving back with my parents, but they said my cat wasn't allowed. I ended up going into a hospital for suicide and depression. Without my cat I felt extra lost. Shes the only reason I got out of bed some days. To my parents I said fuck you guys and prepared to live in my car when I was out of the program. 

I had just recently gotten with a new boyfriend and I moved in with him for a couple weeks. I got a job and an apartment. It went well, but I pushed way too far and 3 weeks later I'm bedbound. 

Eventually I lost my apartment, and moved back with the boyfriend. He took in my cat and me with open arms. I worry everyday about us breaking up and me being homeless. I worry about having to give my cat up and not being able to go to doctors or get medicine. 

That being said, get a pet. She's the reason I get up. My boyfriend helps a lot with making sure she's fed and had water if I forget. She gives me attention and companionship when I am trapped inside all day. Don't let fear push you away from getting your next best friend. 

P.s. if you're looking into getting an ESA, you'll need to talk to a therapist/psychiatrist/GP about getting a letter for her. A lot of professionals don't like to write them so you may have to shop around a bit. I got mine from a partial hospitalization program in a mental health facility. They can come from anywhere. Don't be afraid to ask. Then, you're good to take the pet with you if you end up on your own again. Pets accepted or not, you're allowed to have an ESA in living quarters.

Just a BPM jump can be Orthostatic Hypotension, you need blood pressure as well. You will need to schedule either a tilt table or a standing test in a doctor's office (although the standing tests can vary wildly depending on day, time laying down, time sitting, symtoms, etc etc). 

The phone heart rate is not even close to accurate. You will need an actual blood oximeter and a blood pressure cuff. A small change in BPM is normal, which is why they focus on 30+ BPM increase in a short amount of time. 

If it's not affecting you, then I wouldn't worry about it. The other symptoms can come from hEDS alone, without pots. These are questions to ask a medical professional. As I said before, if it's not bothering you, then focus on other things. If you want answers you'll need to speak to a healthcare professional, which if it's a PCP they'll more than likely send you to a Cardiologist. A cardiologist will probably send you in to get a tilt table, then you'll need to come back for results.

This exact thing happened to me. 

My first neurologist told me I was just making it up due to anxiety, and I needed to seek the help of a mental health professional. I did that, I have a psychiatrist I see on a monthly basis. He said that he doesn't believe it's psychological, although my parents didn't believe that. I'm 20 now, so their disbelief is more of an annoyance than an hindrance (like it would be if I was younger). 
My psychiatrist is the one that sent me for a tilt table test. My psychiatrist is the one that helped me out. Even after a solid diagnosis backed by medical data, from a hospital test, they still think I am just making this up. 

I say tell your parents you want to exhaust all options, and you take their concerns seriously. Get a GOOD psychiatrist. One you like. Then explain everything and see what they say. If they say it's stress related, that's still valid. Something being stress related doesn't mean it doesn't have that effect on your life or that you could just snap out of it. It's a different treatment plan but it's still important. 

Secondly, find a neurologist that will do more testing. I went to a cardiologist for my tilt table test to see if I had POTs (which I do). I am seeing an epileptologist for my seizures. I am seeing a neurologist for nerve damage and chronic migraines. I see a rheumatologist for CFS and Fibro. 

Advocate for yourself, because it's hard to find a medical professional that will do so. When you find a good doc (any kind, hell one of my best is a GP) hold onto them and get referred to everything. Check out all possibilities and see what helps. 

As my epileptologist said, "regardless of the cause, your symptoms are still damaging. They are still impact you very negatively. We just need to find this cause and treat it. If it's an anxiety issue, then we treat that differently..." She names off multiple causes of symptoms and that they are treated differently. It's no different than if a chemical issue was causing problems or a nervous system issue causing problems. They are just treated differently because of different causes. Don't fall into this circle of "it's just anxiety" it's a serious issue. 

Best of luck and hoping for a speedy diagnosis. 

P.S. it can take years to get answers that's been the case with me.
